items.note: K1 states the eight-row schedule, the net y_S <- y_S + x_S for arbitrary scratch values and the three-stage exchange (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a) with restored scratch; K1.1-K1.4 follow the proof at 741-765 (net change (JV+RG)x, bit and complex coefficients, composition of stages). The plan never gives h=100, N, m, the neighbour counts or the wire counts W_b, W_c (767-783), but these are not needed to prove the lemma itself.

K2 states D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} with one frame per gate and edge cost D_v D_u^{-1}. Its method (the invariant that the stored array is the frame applied to the logical array), the gate-commutation step K2.1 and the signed-route corollary K2.2 are the paper's argument at 804-825.

The lemma's content is stated correctly: comparable nondegenerate labels, central 3->4 edges as the only decreasing edges each losing h, L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L, orthonormal residual bases over F_2, and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. The derivation omits the construction that the proof checks: A, P, B, Q, the stage transitions (911-937), the gate-label table eq:motif-labels (975-988) and the residual table (1021-1043). It also never says that F^{tensor 3} has dimension m.

K4 assigns P_U to gates and sinks and -P_{U_a} to sources, then derives s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b < W_b m and the endpoint identity I_m. K4.1-K4.4 reproduce the proof at 1156-1172, including the rank-one exception 2P_{U_a} on the N source edges. The shear frames Phi_M appear in K7.2.2-K7.2.3.

Phase frames, one kernel aI+bX_v (or its inverse) per orthonormal residual vector, s_c = W_c m - 2N + 2L_c, and C^{tensor m} on every role after corrections are all stated. The sub-steps follow 1232-1314: mod-4 weight additivity, odd weight giving the phase, H diag(1,-1) H = X, and the X_a->Y_a pair with Z_{a,k} and i^{27k} corrections.

Correct values: L/N < 1/2 (K3.5); deficits N - 2L_b > 0 and 2N - 2L_c > 0; eta_b and eta_c above 20*2^-50; log m < 20; and m^{1-2^-50} > m(1-20*2^-50) > m(1-eta), giving s/W < m^tau with tau = sigma = 1-2^-50. This is the paper's computation at 1319-1346.

S1 lists the four elementary O(V) operations correctly. S2's claim says a controlled shift costs O(V) without the hypothesis that the offset can be prepared in b^{O(1)} time; that hypothesis appears only in its quote. The claim also omits the coprimality conditions on the units (557-560). Both are infer steps with no sub-steps, so the presence is stated only.

Factorization E_1 Pi E_2, linear-time triangular transforms, conjugation, and one interchange per one of Pi follow 1375-1447 step by step. The statement omits the setting of Lemma lem:matrix-shear: arithmetic over Z/q^b for a fixed odd prime q chosen to avoid the denominators and the diagonal numerators (1396-1404, 1413-1423). That choice is only implicit in K7.1.2's 'diagonal unit'.

Every element of the proof is present: the row split into W role streams of volume V/W, Phi_{A_e} on each edge by recursive pivot interchanges, the endpoint Phi_{I_m}, the three-shear interchange, s calls giving F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1} + O(1), the geometric sum O(e^tau), and the LIFO fixed-tape schedule.

The statement matches lem:chunk-swap. The sub-steps follow 1650-1734: top rho digits as the row field with R = q^{2rho} >= W^k, padding to R', base-m pieces with sum O(Ve^tau), and padding binary ranges to [q^e]. The unequal-width variant appears later, in S8.1.11 and S9.3.8.

The sub-steps reproduce the paper: the C identities, conjugation by P_M with the residual basis as the first columns, one child per basis vector on the f axes of a slot, the inverse child via Z wrappers, at most m(m-1)+3m row additions, exactly s_c children, and H_0^{tensor D} = b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D.

These steps follow the paper's route: eight packed additions, guard interval and bad set, delta_bad, T_0 S_0^{-1} permuting B, swaps and rotations, the radix-sort repair, and the time bound. One step is missing: the shifts handle only j_0..j_{f-2}, and the top selected position j_{f-1} is done separately by a two-bit XOR (2054, 2187-2193). The plan never mentions this, and K8.2.2 says the shifts equal the ideal XORs.

These steps follow the paper. Individual kernels cost O(Ve), node overhead is O(V((eK)^tau+1)), and the q_0 row chunks form a row index split as u=Wg+w. The recurrence F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m) + O((eK)^tau+1) is unrolled to internal O(e^lambda) plus leaves O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}), and the base-m pieces give O(d^{lambda'}).

Stated: Q_p(Hz) in O(Vd^{lambda'}) time, error below sqrt2 2^-p, and exact evaluation with Delta = ceil(C_0 d^{C_1}) = o(p) guard bits. The derivation follows the paper: A(e) <= sA(e/m)+E with E=64(W+m+1)^3, then A(e) <= 8B^2 d^{nu+1}, then the depth-to-width argument, uniform packed-call cost, conversion via H_0 = bSCS, and the row-sum-one contraction with a single truncation.

The steps cover character cancellation by pairing summands, decimation in frequency, bit-reversed storage B_t, grouped rounds H then J_E, the layout L (prefix moves plus chunk exchanges), and the costs O(TpdK), O(Tp pK^{tau-1}) and O(Tp ell d^{lambda'}). They also cover the truncation commuting with J_E and the exact operators LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}. All match 2819-3200.

The signed Kronecker route at B_0 = 2^{4p} is reproduced step by step: evaluation bound, separation |h_j| < B_0/2, carries in {-1,0} and {0,1}, residual identity, final carry, negacyclic reduction, truncation, and the O(rp log(rp)) cost.

Correct error sqrt2 M(3ell+1) 2^-p and cost. The derivation uses the convolution identity with F^+F^- = I/M, P(LBu,LBv) = LB P(u,v), the error chain 2delta+eta then 3delta+eta then times M, and M = T/r products, as at 3414-3495.

The statement includes the identity, the error p^2 and the time O(tp^{3/2+delta} alpha). The proof is reproduced: TP_sF_s = P_tF_tS, the Neumann inverse of N, the normalization 2^{-2alpha^2}, the error and time table, the selector C, the permutations kept inside the identity, tensoring, the line count, and axis exposure O(Tpd^2(1+ell^tau)).

Chirp periodicity and the coefficient computation (S8.2) are as in the paper. So are F_q^+ R_c = R_c^{-1} F_q^+, RF^+R = F^+ with the permutation commuting with pointwise products, the convolution rule giving (u*v)/S^2, and conjugation for RF^+, all at 3938-3987.

Exponents, sizes, box, prime interval, distinct odd primes, T/2 < S < T, alpha^4 theta_i > p and the n^{o(1)} search are correct and match 4049-4171. Some hypotheses of the layer and transform lemmas are only asserted ('chosen with room to spare'), not shown: the inequalities at 4018-4036, the comparison bands a_d, b_d, a_r, b_r, C_ell (4073-4087), and gamma <= b/4 from eq:gamma.

These steps follow 4204-4292: the isomorphism argument via the order of the image of x, the triangular formula with its justification, the padding scan, the update order d..1, the valid-interval rotations preserving the padding, the prefix-controlled cyclic shifts, and unequal-width axis exchanges with total cost O(Tp d^2(1+ell^tau)).

This is the paper's argument: a well-defined diagonal isomorphism preserving the sup norm, the wrap check zeta^{k+l}(-1)^h = zeta^j, M_C = D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g) = (f*g)/T, the computed twist sequence, and twist errors below 4.

Correct as in the paper: the chirp transform, the source transform with exact counterpart 2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A = RF_s, the conjugate opposite procedure, digit scaling by 2^{-b-2}, and the six steps. The roles of the two scalings by S match 4536-4541.

The error chain E_ring < 5TL, then 6TL, then 8TL, then E_s = 9*2^gamma TL, then 2E_s+2 and 3E_s+2, then E_w < 28*2^gamma T^2 L, then the final bound 448b 2^{-b+gamma} < 1/2 matches 4582-4727. The rounding, carry bound, carry invariant and 2n-bit output match 4728-4806.

The steps cover all seven table rows with their powers of p, the margins g_1..g_7 with min 2^-181 = 2 kappa, setup costs o(Tp), compact exceptional sorting o(V), absorption of log p, and the schoolbook cutoff, as at 4815-4995.
S0 says the bound disproves the n log n optimality conjecture. It never gives the liminf T_A(n)/(n lg n) = 0 criterion or the eventual-lower-bound formulation in the fixed-tape model (381-387).

errors.says: The pairing <t_S,t_T> = |S cap T| - 1 is given for both label spaces: 'rational form I-J/9 for the bit network, the dot product on F_2^h for the complex one'.
errors.paper: The formula |S cap T| - 1, with <t_T,t_T> = 2, holds for the rational form I-J/9. For the complex network the label space is F_2^h with the ordinary dot product, where t_S.t_T = |S cap T| mod 2 and t_T.t_T = 1. Orthogonality there comes from neighbours having even intersection.

errors.says: Every nonzero binary orthogonal residual is nonalternating because 'it contains a norm-one coordinate vector'.
errors.paper: The norm-one vector is built by tensoring chosen norm-one vectors in each factor, including the triple-indicator tensors that span P and Q, and placing the result in one orthogonal summand. In general it is not a coordinate vector.

errors.says: Both tape procedures cost F_k = O(e^tau) per unit volume with tau < 1.
errors.paper: Only the interchange recurrence gives F_k = O(e^tau) (1552-1557). The butterfly-layer recurrence F(e) <= (s/W)F(e/m) + O((eK)^tau + 1) has a growing node overhead and gives O(e^lambda) internally, with leaves O(e^sigma d^{beta(1-sigma)}) and O(d^{lambda'}) overall. The plan's own K8.3 states this correctly.

errors.says: A controlled update y -> y + a(controls) mod Q, and multiplication by a fixed unit, costs O(V). The claim states no condition on the offset.
errors.paper: The O(V) bound needs the offset to be preparable in b^{O(1)} time from the controls, each control used in an offset of O(b) digits, and the units to have numerators and denominators prime to q.

errors.says: Outside the bad set the packed shifts equal the ideal XORs.
errors.paper: The shifts act only on the segments at j_0..j_{f-2}, so S_0 agrees with the T_0 that XORs those positions. The top position j_{f-1} is omitted from the shifts and done afterwards by a separate two-bit XOR.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}): the rank saving s < Wm becomes the interchange recurrence (K7) and the butterfly-layer recurrence (K8), which give the transform costs (S6), convolution (S7), resampling and chirp (S8), assembly with exact recovery (S9), and the cost table with min margin 2 kappa (S10). Every link from s < Wm to the final exponent is present. The plan thins out at the start: it never fixes h=100, N = binom(h,3)^3 or m = h^3, and it asserts the subspace labels and the parameter conditions without the paper's label tables or exponent inequalities.

steps.note: The exchange network itself is fully given: the eight-row schedule, (X_a,Y_a) -> (-Y_a,X_a) and restored scratch. None of the defining sizes appear: h=100, the indexing of X_a,Y_a by triples of triples, N = binom(h,3)^3 and m = h^3. N and m are used as symbols but never defined, so I choose the conservative verdict.
A common invertible frame per gate commutes with the pointwise gate, so the network implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} and each edge pays only D_v D_u^{-1}.

Nondegenerate subspaces of F^{tensor 3} built from triple indicators, comparable labels on every edge, and central-wire 3->4 edges as the only decreasing ones, each losing P tensor F of dimension h. The dimension m of the ambient space is not stated.
P_V - P_U has rank dim V - dim U; the N source edges are the exceptions, with matrix 2P_{U_a} of rank one.
Sum of |Delta dim| = Wm - 2N + 2L with L = Ich, by telescoping at gates with source sum N and sink sum Wm - N; then s_b = W_b m - N + 2L_b.
L_b/N = 100/539 and L_c/N = 101/539, both below 1/2, so the deficits N - 2L_b > 0 and 2N - 2L_c > 0 give s < Wm.

M_sink(rho(w)) - M_source(w) = I_m on every role (P_{U_a^perp} + P_{U_a} for X_a; 0 and I elsewhere), so with frames Phi_M the network gives Phi_{I_m}, the shear H <- H + D on every row including scratch rows.
A rank-a shear factors as E_1 Pi E_2 and costs exactly a interchanges plus O(V); each pivot interchange is a recursive call, so a node makes s calls in all.
Role streams have volume V/W, so F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1} + O(1). s/W < m^tau with tau = 1-2^-50 comes from eta > 20*2^-50 and log m < 20, and the geometric sum gives F_k = O(e^tau).

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the central saving from the frame principle through the label budget, the rank-equals-dimension-change rule with the N rank-one source exceptions, the strict deficit from L/N < 1/2, the endpoint shear, the factorization into a recursive calls per rank-a edge, and the recurrence with tau = 1-2^-50. The only weak step is the starting network (C1): its exchange behaviour is given in full, but the defining sizes h=100, N = binom(h,3)^3 and m = h^3 are never stated.
